name: Greywalk Flatboot
description: A flat-soled ankle boot in grey synth-leather so cheap it creases white at every flex point. The seams are factory-done but barely — threads already pulling at the toe box on a new pair. Popular because they're one of the cheapest new-manufactured boots available, sold in bulk at Shelf market stalls. Most people buy two pairs at once knowing one will fail within months.
what_it_says: You're not pretending. These are what you could afford, and you're not making excuses.
worn_by: people just arriving in the city
story_hooks: Greywalk is a front company. Someone's tracking purchase data from every stall that sells them.
A pair still has the original sales tag — purchased the same day a person disappeared.
